Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The test `testIssue631` fails when solving for the root of the function `f(x) = exp(x) - pi^3` over the interval [1, 10] using the `RegulaFalsiSolver`. There is a reported failure in the "RegulaFalsiSolver" solver when running a similar test.

The `RegulaFalsiSolver` constructor calls its superclass constructor with a specific method type `REGULA_FALSI` and a default or provided accuracy. The actual solving logic most likely resides in the `doSolve()` method, but this method is not visible directly in `RegulaFalsiSolver`; it may be inherited or abstract.

The root cause can be inferred as an issue with the implementation of the regula falsi method in the solver. The method typically refines the bracket for the root by linearly interpolating and may fail or get stuck under certain function shapes, possibly causing infinite loops or failure to converge. The test performs 3624 iterations (or maximum evaluations), indicating the solver struggles to reach the solution within that limit.

The recent bug reports do not appear relevant to this failure; they relate to normalization issues or constructors of unrelated classes.

Hence, the problem likely stems from the `RegulaFalsiSolver` implementation of the root-finding algorithm, where the regula falsi method may fail to converge or not bracket correctly and thus fail the test.

Next steps would involve examining the detailed implementation of the regula falsi algorithm in the `RegulaFalsiSolver`, especially in its root-finding loop or update steps (likely in a `doSolve()` or equivalent method). This would clarify why the algorithm fails to converge or completes within the allowed number of iterations for the given function in the test.

The initial diagnosis is that the Regula Falsi method implementation in `RegulaFalsiSolver` is flawed or incomplete, causing it to fail convergence and break the test.

Candidates for fixes are methods implementing the solving/iteration logic of `RegulaFalsiSolver`.

Suggested methods to inspect/fix include:
- `org.apache.commons.math.analysis.solvers.RegulaFalsiSolver.doSolve()` (or equivalent root finding method)
- If `RegulaFalsiSolver` extends a base solver class with the solving loop, then that loop method in the base class also needs inspection.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
